messages:
Incident Bot: PAGER -> Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-7 has sustained p99 > 2s for /v1/generate for the last 6m. p95 has climbed from 480ms to ~1.2s. Queue depth: 230. Streaming stall rate up 4x. Trigger: latency_slo_breach.
Alice W: seeing the same in console — streaming sessions are getting stalled around token 120-250. p99 token-lat latency looks like long warmup on new workers. First saw spike ~07:12 UTC.
Ben P: pulling logs from autoscaler and pool manager. looks like new nodes request -> kernels load -> handshake timeouts. autoscaler reported warmup_ok after ~45s but handshake window is 30s so many requests hit fallback queue. snippet: ```2026-03-15T07:12:34Z pool-manager INFO starting worker w-7c12, allocate gpu g4dn.x8; 07:12:35 kernel-loader INFO loading int8 kernels -> 28s; 07:12:59 handshake WARN client handshake timed out (30s)```
Carla M: queue depth correlate: hotshot onboarding bursts (mobile app release) + burst-routing policy routed extra traffic to dedicated-7. Warmup capacity ~= 0 available for that model variant.
Alice W: customer impact -> Support flagged 3 live customers: acme-fin, writewise, draftly. Reports: SSE disconnects, stalled streams, slow completions. We've got ~12 support tickets open.
Oncall Pager: paging Dave R on-call now. Dave, can you join? We may need manual capacity and routing changes.
Dave R: on it. quick question: do we have spare dedicated pools in eu-west that can accept the variant? Also what's the acceptable mitigation: reduce quality (quantized model) or route to hosted?
Ben P: spare pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 has 40% idle. But it's pinned to a different model family; we can route if we enable model-compat fallback. Risk: slight cost spike and regen quality drop for some customers.
Carla M: recommended mitigations in order: 1) temporarily route incoming burst traffic for model redwood-v2-large -> redwood-v2-medium-quant on eu-west-1-dedicated-3 for new sessions; 2) manual scale + preheat 2 workers in dedicated-7 with warmed KV/prefix cache; 3) enable streaming backpressure to shed >500 concurrent SSEs for low-tier customers; 4) notify customers in parallel.
Alice W: I'll open an incident banner and notify support. Ben, can you run the warmup commands to prewarm two workers? Use the warmup script to prepopulate KV and load kernels.
Ben P: executing now. command: ```./infra/tools/prewarm_worker --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-7 --count 2 --model redwood-v2-large --kv-seed /preheat/prefixes-07-12.json && sleep 5 && infractl pool check-health dedicated-7``` Will post output.
Ben P: prewarm logs: ```prewarm: spawn worker w-7c14 ok; kernel load time 19s; kv seed done; health: serving(true)``` But note one worker failed kernel init first attempt (OOM during kernel compile) then retried and succeeded. That's contributing to the transient delay.
Dave R: I'm going to manually route 30% of incoming traffic for redwood-v2-large to eu-west-1-dedicated-3 (quant fallback) and pin canary to low-risk customers. Doing it now.
Dave R: routing change applied via routing-api: ```POST /admin/route -> {from: 'eu-west-1-dedicated-7', to: 'eu-west-1-dedicated-3', model_fallback: 'redwood-v2-medium-quant', percent: 30}``` -> 200 OK.
Incident Bot: action recorded: manual routing change by Dave R.
Alice W: Support banner draft: "We are investigating intermittent latency and streaming stalls affecting some users in EU. Engineers are mitigating and we will update in 15 minutes." Posting now. :rotating_light:
Carla M: Also increased autoscaler warmup timeout to 60s for dedicated pools (temp) so handshake doesn't prematurely fail while kernels compile. Patch applied to pool-manager config: ```max_handshake_wait: 60s```
Ben P: monitoring - p95 dropped from 1.2s to ~650ms within 90s after routing + prewarm. p99 down to ~1.1s. Queue depth down from 230 -> 80. Streaming stall rate halved.
Oncall Pager: customers acme-fin and draftly reported partial recovery for in-progress sessions, writewise still seeing intermittent stalls.
Dave R: I'm taking the incident for rotation. Handing off to SRE Rotation. Summary: dedicated-7 saturated during a traffic burst; autoscaler warmup + kernel compile delays caused handshake timeouts -> backlog and streaming stalls. Mitigations applied: manual prewarm (2 workers), temporary routing to dedicated-3 quant fallback (30%), increased handshake wait to 60s, soft backpressure for low-tier traffic.
SRE Rotation: acknowledged. I'll keep the channel updated and own postmortem. Immediate next steps: 1) continue monitoring p95/p99 for 30m; 2) collect kernel compile failure logs (Ben); 3) run headroom test to confirm safe scaleback; 4) schedule follow-up with model-onboarding team re: compile OOMs.
Alice W: I've added an incident tracker entry and assigned tasks: #1 alerts runbook, #2 customer comms, #3 infra hotfix (handshake wait), #4 postmortem.
Carla M: quick root-cause hypothesis for postmortem: simultaneous hotshot onboarding + kernel compile OOM/retries + autoscaler handshake timeout (30s) -> effectively reduced warmup throughput. Need long-term fix: 1) increase default warmup window or ensure kernel precompilation during model upload; 2) improve preheat capacity prediction for hotshot bursts; 3) add auto-fallback path to hosted when sustained handshake failures detected.
Dave R: I'm leaving the hot channel; SRE Rotation has ownership. If p99 creeps back up >1.5s or queue >150, page me immediately.
SRE Rotation: will run three checks and update every 10m. Current status: mitigations holding, customer impact reduced. Postmortem ETA EOD.
Oncall Pager: closing active page for primary on-call; monitor-only alerts remain. :white_check_mark:
Alice W: thanks everyone — keeping incident banner up until confirmed stable for 1h.
Incident Bot: incident status -> mitigation_in_progress; recorded actions: routing change, handshake_timeout_patch, prewarm workers.
SRE Rotation: final note before we archive: include timeline and command runbook in postmortem, and add a test in chaos harness for kernel-compile slowdown during autoscale.
Dave R: noted. end of handoff.
